findings.title: None receipt from gateway is indistinguishable from an unclaimed key, so the retry charges again
findings.evidence: begin() returns self._completed[key] (which may be None) and charge_once treats a None return as 'no prior charge': '    if prior is not None:' then proceeds to gateway.charge. A gateway whose charge() returns None (stub, 204-style response, mis-wired adapter) gets None stored by 'self._completed[key] = receipt', and every subsequent call with the same key is charged a second time - the exact failure the module exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit sentinel (for example a module-level MISSING object, or have begin return a tuple of (found, receipt)) so a stored None receipt still short-circuits. Additionally reject a None gateway receipt in complete()/charge_once (raise instead of storing it) so a misbehaving gateway fails loudly rather than corrupting the dedup table.

findings.title: Same key reused with a different amount or currency silently returns the old receipt
findings.evidence: The prior receipt is returned without comparing amount_cents or currency against the original request: '        return prior'. charge_once(store, gw, 5000, 'usd', key) after a completed 1000-cent charge returns the 1000-cent receipt, and a caller that only checks for a receipt will record a 5000-cent payment that never happened (or ship goods priced at the second amount).
findings.recommendation: Persist the request fingerprint (amount_cents and currency) alongside the receipt and raise a dedicated conflict error when a repeat key arrives with different parameters, matching common payment-API idempotency semantics; only return the stored receipt when the fingerprint matches.

findings.title: Completed-receipt table grows without bound; no expiry or eviction
findings.evidence: Every completed charge is retained forever in the process: '            self._completed[key] = receipt'. A long-lived service accepts unbounded unique idempotency keys, so both _completed and the transient _in_flight set need a TTL/eviction policy (payment providers expire keys after ~24h), otherwise memory grows monotonically and stale keys suppress legitimate future charges.
findings.recommendation: Add an insertion timestamp per key and prune entries older than a configured retention window (on write, or via a periodic sweep under the existing lock).

findings.title: In-flight claim has no expiry, so a stalled gateway call poisons the key permanently
findings.evidence: The key is claimed and only released by complete() or abandon(): '            self._in_flight.add(key)'. If gateway.charge never returns (no timeout on the HTTP client), the key stays in flight forever and every later retry raises DuplicateRequestInFlight until the process restarts; the caller also gets an immediate exception with no way to observe the in-flight request's eventual outcome.
findings.recommendation: Record a claim timestamp and allow re-claiming (or re-attempt against the gateway, which is idempotent by key) once the claim exceeds a timeout; alternatively expose the in-flight state so callers can retry-later instead of treating DuplicateRequestInFlight as a hard failure.

findings.title: Idempotency state is process-local; cross-restart dedup relies on unverified gateway behaviour
findings.evidence: The store is a plain dict: '        self._completed = {}'. After a crash or restart the record of a completed charge is gone, and the docstring's claim that a retry is deduplicated by the provider assumes the injected gateway actually honours idempotency_key - nothing in charge_once verifies or documents that as a hard requirement, and a gateway ignoring the key charges twice.
findings.recommendation: Either back the store with durable storage (DB row keyed by idempotency_key with the receipt) or make the provider-side dedup an explicit, documented contract of the gateway interface and state it as a precondition in the charge_once docstring.

findings.title: No tests for the double-charge, concurrency, or failure paths
findings.evidence: The diff adds a payment-deduplication entry point with zero accompanying tests: 'def charge_once(store, gateway, amount_cents, currency, idempotency_key):'. Untested behaviours include the exception path that calls abandon(), concurrent begin() raising DuplicateRequestInFlight (with a second thread that must not reach the gateway), repeat calls with mismatched amounts, and gateways returning None or raising after a successful charge.
findings.evidence_quote: def charge_once(store, gateway, amount_cents, currency, idempotency_key):
findings.recommendation: Add tests with a fake gateway that counts charge() calls: concurrent same-key calls must result in exactly one gateway call, exception paths must release the in-flight key, completed keys must never reach the gateway, and a None/mismatched receipt must fail rather than double charge.
